messages:
Maya Chen: Heads up — acme-inc (enterprise) opened a support ticket: sudden increase in 5xx and timeouts for hosted inference since the 08:05 deploy. spike in gateway 502/504s and client latency. link to ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/12345
Samir Patel: Looking at the metrics now. Which roll/flag was in the deploy? any canary targets?
Maya Chen: Canary was 10% on the new kernel switch. I think ops flipped a config flag: `kernel_selector: kernel_v2` and `prefetch_window: 64` on canary slice. Timeline: deploy at 08:04, errors start 08:12 UTC.
Jules Ortega: Confirmed in config history: `feature/serve-kernel-v2` flag set to true for slice A at 08:03:50. I can see error rate diverging on slice A nodes vs baseline.
Samir Patel: Can you paste a quick failing request/response? need headers and body if possible.
Maya Chen: From support logs (redacted):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Customer: acme-inc" -d '{"input":"test"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
> HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
> Server: gateway
> Content-Length: 58
{
  "error": "upstream read timeout",
  "detail": "kvcache read timed out"
}
```
Samir Patel: That upstream read timeout plus kvcache hint points at kernel_v2 path touching an incompatible KV cache encoding; requests that hit KV cold path are timing out and cascading as 502s from gateway. Also seeing auth handshake latencies higher on those hosts (possibly extra RTT).
Evelyn King: We need rollback ASAP and a clear customer note. Samir, can you propose rollback steps? Li, please stand by to execute.
Samir Patel: Rollback plan: 1) Flip `kernel_selector` back to `kernel_v1` for the canary slice via config-service; 2) Reduce prefetch_window to 32; 3) Scale canary pods to zero if flip doesn't take effect quickly. Command (config-service):
```
configctl set --slice canaryA kernel_selector=kernel_v1 prefetch_window=32 --reason "hotfix: revert kernel_v2 after 5xx spike"
```
Li Wang: Executing now. Running `configctl`...
infra-bot: deploybot: config update started for slice canaryA by Li Wang at 08:33:05 UTC
Li Wang: `configctl` returned: OK -> change queued, propagation expected ~30s to config-service replicas.
Samir Patel: Watching logs. If 502s don't drop in 2 mins, we'll scale canary pods down and force a rollback in the rollout service.
Maya Chen: Notifying acme-inc support contact now (short note + ETA).
support-bot: support: note posted to ticket #12345: "We observed a canary config flip that likely caused API 502s. Rolling back now; will follow up when rates return to normal."
Li Wang: config propagation complete. infra-bot: deploybot: config update completed at 08:34:12 UTC.
Samir Patel: Seeing immediate drop in 5xx on canaryA hosts. Error rate back to baseline at 08:36 UTC. Latency returning to normal.
Maya Chen: Messaging customer: we've rolled back the canary flag and are seeing error rates return to normal. Please let us know if you continue to see errors.
Evelyn King: Action items: 1) Samir to file a postmortem explaining why kernel_v2 interacts poorly with current KV encoding and add an automated canary guard for kvcache latency. 2) Jules to add verification step to rollout that validates KV read latency under load before promoting. 3) Support to send final update to acme-inc and close ticket when stable.
Samir Patel: I'll own the postmortem. Initial hypothesis: config gating wasn't strict enough — we promoted kernel branch without ensuring backward-compatible kvcache encoding or adequate canary perf checks.
Jules Ortega: Also add a telemetry alert: if canary 5xx > baseline + 0.5% for 3 consecutive mins, auto-flip flag to previous.
Maya Chen: Thanks team. Closing incident channel when ticket confirmed closed.
infra-bot: alerting: incident resolved (monitoring) — 5xx spike subsided, rolling averages normal at 08:42 UTC
Li Wang: Confirmed final check at 08:44 UTC, all canary hosts green.
support-bot: ticket #12345 updated: "Root cause suspected misapplied kernel flag; rolled back; monitoring green. Will follow up with postmortem link."
Evelyn King: Good coordination. Follow-up: schedule postmortem review, assign owners for automation.
